disclaimer: This is a constructed sample, not Stripe data. Fraud is overrepresented so the lag is visible in a short demo. In live card payments, fraud is closer to 1 in 1,000.

features.label: Card age
features.raise_when: A newer card usually raises risk.

features.label: Email age
features.raise_when: A newer email usually raises risk.

features.label: Cards seen on this IP
features.raise_when: Many cards on one IP usually raises risk.

features.label: Amount
features.raise_when: Very small test charges, or amounts far from a card's usual size, can raise risk.

features.label: Charges in the last hour
features.raise_when: A burst of charges usually raises risk.

features.label: Clean history on other merchants
features.raise_when: A long clean history usually lowers risk. That is also how late-reported fraud hides.

features.label: First time at this merchant
features.raise_when: A first charge at this merchant, especially with a long history elsewhere, can raise risk.

features.label: Billing and IP country differ
features.raise_when: A country mismatch usually raises risk.

features.label: Throwaway-style email
features.raise_when: A disposable or patterned email usually raises risk.

features.label: Merchant's recent dispute rate
features.raise_when: A higher merchant dispute rate usually raises risk.

feature_columns.label: Name and email do not match
Clean history elsewhere, first time here

now.name: Fit now, with the labels you have
now.blurb: Train on every payment in the 10-week window, using only the fraud reports that had arrived by training day. Recent weeks count more, so the model can chase new attacks, and also so immature labels can do more damage.

wait.name: Train only on mature weeks
wait.blurb: Drop the most recent 6 weeks and train only on payments that are old enough for most disputes to have arrived. Labels are more trustworthy. The window is smaller and a little stale.
